# Review: Site Development and Hosting Agreement — HDI (vendor) / Deerskin (customer)

**Bottom line:** The commercial deal (HDI builds, hosts and promotes at its cost for a revenue share) is attractive, but the risk allocation is unusually thin for a hosting/e-commerce agreement. The three things I would not sign as-is are (1) the Termination Payment formula, (2) the total absence of service levels, indemnities, IP/exit rights and any liability framework, and (3) the confidentiality/data provisions, which don't survive termination and don't restrain HDI's use of our customer data. Deerskin is also being asked to shut down its existing Globix hosting before it has any assurance the HDI site works.

---

## Priority 1 — Do not sign without changes

### 1. Termination Payment (§4.2) — effectively a perpetual lock-in

**Issue.** The payment is `(trailing 12-month Net Sales − $800,000) ÷ 2`. At $2M of Net Sales that is a $600,000 exit fee — roughly a full year of HDI's revenue share (30% of Net Sales over $11k/month ≈ $560k on the same numbers). Worse:
- It is triggered by *any* termination "by the Company," which under §4.1 includes ordinary non-renewal on 90 days' notice. Deerskin can therefore never exit without paying.
- It is not carved out for termination for HDI's material breach, insolvency, non-performance, or chronic downtime. We would pay HDI for HDI's failure.
- It is measured on **revenue**, not margin, and includes shipping/handling — it can exceed our gross profit on those sales.
- There is no reciprocal payment if HDI walks (HDI may terminate on 90 days' notice and owes nothing, leaving us with no site).

**Fix.**
- Limit to termination *for convenience by the Company during the initial term only*; expressly exclude (i) non-renewal at any anniversary on notice, (ii) termination for HDI breach/insolvency/SLA failure/§1.6 launch failure, (iii) termination following HDI change of control, and (iv) expiration.
- Convert the formula to a fee-based measure and cap it: e.g., "an amount equal to the fees payable under §3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date," or at minimum cap the current formula at a hard dollar number.
- State it is HDI's **sole and exclusive remedy** for early termination, is subject to Deerskin's right of set-off, and is non-accelerating.
- Confirm §1.6's "without penalty" language expressly overrides §4.2.

Suggested insert to §4.2(a): *"...provided that no Termination Payment shall be due if the Company terminates or elects not to renew (i) upon or effective as of any anniversary of the Effective Date, (ii) for HDI's material breach (uncured for 30 days), (iii) for HDI's failure to meet the service levels in Exhibit A, (iv) under Section 1.6, or (v) upon HDI's insolvency or change of control."*

### 2. No service levels, no remedies, no exit/transition rights

**Issue.** §§1.3–1.4 promise a server and "shared but greater than T-1 bandwidth" — no uptime commitment, no response/repair times, no peak-season capacity commitment, no backup/disaster recovery, no security obligations, no maintenance windows, no reporting. Our only stated remedy anywhere is the §1.6 launch-date termination right. Because HDI is paid on revenue share, downtime costs HDI 30 cents on the dollar and costs us the other 70 plus brand damage.

**Fix.** Add an SLA exhibit: ≥99.5% monthly availability (excluding scheduled windows), severity-based response/resolution times, nightly backups with defined RPO/RTO, capacity for peak (Q4) volumes, monthly performance reports, and a termination right (with no Termination Payment) for two SLA failures in any rolling six months. Add HDI responsibility for its subcontractors and prior notice of any platform/hosting migration.

### 3. Exit is catastrophic: no IP ownership, domain, data-portability or transition assistance

**Issue.** HDI builds and hosts the Site; the Agreement never says who owns the site design, code, configuration, or the **URL** (which §5.1 has HDI register). On termination we have no license, no code, no domain, no customer/order data export, and no transition assistance — and we may owe a six-figure Termination Payment. Meanwhile §9(b) requires us to terminate Globix, so we will have no fallback platform.

**Fix.** Add an IP/exit section:
- Deerskin owns all Content, the Marks, all Site customer and order data, and the domain name (registered in Deerskin's name; HDI to transfer/authorize transfer at our request and automatically on termination).
- Deerskin owns (or receives a perpetual, royalty-free license to) all Site-specific design, look-and-feel, HTML/creative and interface deliverables; HDI retains its pre-existing platform tools but grants a wind-down license.
- On expiration/termination for any reason: HDI provides up to 180 days' transition assistance at agreed rates, delivers all Deerskin data (including customer, order and abandoned-cart data) in a mutually usable format, and thereafter deletes/returns it and ceases all use of the Marks.

### 4. No indemnities, no warranties on the services, no liability framework

**Issue.** §9 contains only corporate-authority reps. There is no warranty that the services will be performed in a professional/workmanlike manner, no non-infringement warranty for HDI's platform, no malicious-code warranty, no compliance-with-law warranty. There are **no indemnities at all** and **no limitation of liability** — meaning unlimited exposure on both sides (including our exposure for an exclusivity or list-use dispute), with no consequential-damages waiver.

**Fix.**
- Add HDI warranties: professional and workmanlike performance; the Site/platform does not infringe third-party IP; no viruses/disabling code; compliance with applicable law (including payment-card and privacy requirements applicable to its systems).
- Add mutual indemnities: HDI indemnifies for third-party IP claims relating to the platform/technology, for security incidents on HDI-hosted systems, and for HDI's negligence/willful misconduct and misuse of Deerskin data or e-mail lists; Deerskin indemnifies for Content and product claims.
- Add a mutual cap (e.g., fees paid/payable in the prior 12 months) and a mutual consequential-damages waiver, with carve-outs for indemnities, confidentiality, IP infringement, data breach, and the Termination Payment.

### 5. Confidentiality does not survive; customer data is unprotected

**Issue.** §10.7 (Survival) lists §§6.3, 7, 9 and 10 — **Section 8 (Confidentiality) is omitted.** Read literally, all confidentiality obligations lapse on termination. Separately, §8 has no return/destruction obligation, no need-to-know limitation, no requirement to bind employees/subcontractors, no notice obligation before a compelled disclosure, no injunctive-relief acknowledgment, and no data-security standard beyond "reasonable measures."

Most importantly, nothing restricts HDI — a large multi-title cataloger with Xoom/Excite promotional relationships — from **using Site customer names, e-mails and purchase data for its own catalogs**. §8.1 nominally captures "user information" as Confidential Information, but confidentiality is not the same as a use restriction, and the 2-year survival cap in §10.7 would gut even that.

**Fix.**
- Add Section 8 to the survival list; make confidentiality survive 5 years (perpetually for trade secrets and customer data), notwithstanding the 2-year cap in §10.7.
- Add an express data clause: all Site user/customer/transaction data is Deerskin Confidential Information and Deerskin property; HDI may use it **solely** to perform under this Agreement; no use for HDI's own or any affiliate's or third party's marketing, list rental, appending, modeling or catalog mailings; no aggregation or de-identified reuse; return/deletion on termination; prompt notice of any unauthorized access.
- Add subcontractor flow-down, compelled-disclosure notice, and an equitable-relief clause.

---

## Priority 2 — Material, should be fixed

**6. Globix / Effective Date timing (§§4.1, 9(b), 1.6).** The Effective Date only occurs when both parties sign a writing confirming the Site is "fully operational" — HDI could withhold that signature indefinitely, and the interaction with §1.6's 60/70-day deadlines (which run from execution) is unclear. Yet we must terminate Globix "on or prior to the Effective Date."
*Fix:* Make the Agreement effective on execution, with a separate defined "Launch Date"; permit Deerskin to keep Globix live in parallel for 60 days post-Launch; condition the Globix termination covenant on the Site having operated in compliance with the SLA for 30 consecutive days; make §1.6's outside date a hard date with no Termination Payment and reimbursement of our reasonable transition costs.

**7. Net Sales / fee definition (§3.1).** "(3016)" is a typo; confirm 30%. The base is over-inclusive: it expressly includes **shipping and handling** (a pass-through to carriers) and does not deduct sales/use tax, discounts and promotional credits, credit-card fees, chargebacks and fraudulent orders, cancelled/undeliverable orders, bad debt, or gift-wrap. Also clarify that 30% applies only to the increment above $11,000 per month (and confirm the threshold does not roll over/aggregate).
*Fix:* Redraft Net Sales to exclude the above; state that refunds/exchanges/chargebacks are deducted in the month taken with a true-up, and that overpayments are credited or refunded within 30 days of quarterly reconciliation.

**8. Audit rights (§3.4) — HDI's own manager inspects our books.** Giving a competitor's General Manager access to Deerskin records is a competitive-information risk.
*Fix:* Audits by an independent CPA (not a competitor, bound by NDA, no contingent fee), once per 12 months, records limited to Net Sales calculation, during term + 12 months, HDI pays unless a shortfall >5% is found. Make the right reciprocal as to HDI's reporting/traffic records.

**9. Exclusivity scope (§6.1) is too broad and internally inconsistent.** "Any project similar to the Site... with respect to Deerskin Products **or products substantially similar** to Deerskin Products" could be read to bar Deerskin from third-party marketplaces, affiliate/portal programs, drop-ship arrangements with retailers, and even sales of comparable leather goods under other names. Also, the sentence grants HDI an "exclusive right to use the 'Deerskin' brand for a self-contained web site" while the next paragraph grants only a **non-exclusive** license — reconcile.
*Fix:* Narrow to "a dedicated, Deerskin-branded direct-to-consumer e-commerce web site offering Deerskin Products." Expressly carve out: closeouts (§6.2), Joan Cook, marketplaces/portals/affiliate and third-party retailer sites, wholesale customers' own sites, catalog/telephone/retail channels, informational or brand sites, and any brand acquired after the date hereof. Define "self-contained."

**10. Trademark license terms (§6.1) are incomplete.** No quality-control or approval right over HDI's use, no acknowledgment that Deerskin owns the Marks and all goodwill, no prohibition on HDI registering the Marks or Mark-containing domains/keywords, and no express termination of the license on termination with a short wind-down.
*Fix:* Add all of the above, plus immediate suspension rights for misuse and a covenant to assign any Mark-containing domain or registration to Deerskin.

**11. Assignment (§10.3) permits free assignment.** HDI could assign this Agreement — including our brand license, our customer data and the exclusivity — to a competitor (the clause even names Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled as competitors).
*Fix:* No assignment or delegation without the other party's prior written consent; narrow permitted-assignee exception excluding competitors; plus Deerskin termination right (no Termination Payment) on HDI change of control.

**12. Promotion commitment (§1.8) is unmeasurable.** "No less favorably than it promotes HDI's catalog titles" is unauditable, and the Xoom/Excite reference has no minimums.
*Fix:* Add a promotion schedule with minimum committed placements/impressions/e-mail inclusions per quarter, reporting, and a termination right without Termination Payment for material failure. This is our principal consideration for the revenue share — it should be enforceable.

**13. Merchant-of-record / order-processing cost allocation (§§2.2, 5.3).** We bear "all costs associated with the processing of customer orders" (undefined) and all merchant-of-record liability — chargebacks, fraud, consumer-protection compliance, and sales/use tax (note HDI's NJ servers may create nexus questions). Yet HDI controls the order-capture and data-transmission pipeline (§1.5) with no accountability for errors.
*Fix:* Define "processing costs" (limit to payment gateway/card fees, fulfillment, customer service); make HDI responsible for losses caused by its errors, mis-pricing, data loss or security failures in the order pipeline; allocate tax-determination responsibility and require HDI to support tax calculation/reporting; require HDI to maintain payment-data security and to notify us of incidents.

**14. E-mail list cross-promotion (§7.1).** "Reciprocal and equitable" is vague, and the clause contemplates a Party's *use of the other Party's* list — a privacy and list-asset risk.
*Fix:* No transfer of lists; each party sends on the other's behalf through its own or its ESP's systems; single-use only, no copying, retention, appending or downstream transfer; compliance with each party's posted privacy policy and applicable law; volume caps and mutual approval (already present); indemnity for misuse.

---

## Priority 3 — Missing standard provisions

Add: force majeure (with a right to terminate for extended outage, no Termination Payment); insurance (commercial general, professional/E&O, and — to the extent available — network security, with certificates); dispute resolution, exclusive venue (NY) and jury waiver; escalation between General Managers before suit; publicity/press-release consent (§8.1 covers confidentiality of terms but note HDI is an SEC filer — add a securities-disclosure carve-out with a request for confidential treatment, and be aware this document was filed as an exhibit); set-off; no third-party beneficiaries; change-control process for Site changes; records retention; compliance with applicable law (both parties); Content license grant to HDI (limited to the Site, during the term); acknowledgment that Deerskin's approvals under §5.2 do not relieve HDI of its performance obligations.

## Cleanup / drafting errors

- §3.1: "thirty percent (3016)" — numeral typo.
- Two sections numbered **10.7** and duplicate downstream numbering; §10.7 (Survival) omits §8 and also omits §§3 (payment true-ups), 4.2 (Termination Payment), and the exit/IP obligations we add.
- §10.7's blanket "two years" survival cap should be qualified ("except as otherwise expressly provided").
- §4.1: clarify whether the 90-day notice may be given at any time (termination for convenience) or only prior to an anniversary (non-renewal) — this drives §4.2 exposure.
- §1.6: 60-day launch deadline runs from execution, but our Content is due 10 days after execution — add a day-for-day extension only for our documented delay, with the outside date otherwise firm.
- §9(b): "provided, that the Globix Agreement is terminated on or prior to the Effective Date" — missing period; also see item 6.

---

### Negotiation posture

Items 1–5 are the walk-away set; they are conventional asks and I would expect HDI to accept most of them. Items 6, 7, 9 and 11 have real dollar value and should be traded together. Because HDI bears all build/hosting cost and earns only on a revenue share, HDI's strongest argument is that it needs the Termination Payment to recover its investment — the right answer is a declining, capped, initial-term-only fee with clean breach carve-outs, not a perpetual percentage-of-revenue exit toll.
